messages.subject: digitsurface mean centers regardless of setting
parts:
Hello!

Quick background - we have four laryngeal cartilages which were micro-ct scanned in anatomical position. The cartilage were then saved as four separate surface files and landmarks / semilandmarks were acquired using various Geomorph functions, including digitsurface. 

Although we set the center=FALSE option, the surface always ends up centered at the origin after using digitsurface.

We are hoping to keep the surfaces in their original global coordinate system so that the four cartilages can then be treated as a single structure for superimposition purposes.

We would appreciate assistance in this.

Here is the code (M20Al and P12Al are ply files):

lm<-digit.fixed(M20Al,12,center=FALSE)

buildtemplate(M20Al,lm,50,center=FALSE) 

LMdata<-digitsurface(P12Al,12, ptsize=1,center=FALSE) 

Thanks in advance!

-Karen

Hello!

 

Quick background - we have four laryngeal cartilages which were micro-ct scanned in anatomical position. The cartilage were then saved as four separate surface files and landmarks / semilandmarks were acquired using various Geomorph functions, including digitsurface. 

 

Although we set the center=FALSE option, the surface always ends up centered at the origin after using digitsurface.

 

We are hoping to keep the surfaces in their original global coordinate system so that the four cartilages can then be treated as a single structure for superimposition purposes.

 

We would appreciate assistance in this.

 

Here is the code (M20Al and P12Al are ply files):

 

lm<-digit.fixed(M20Al,12,center=FALSE)

 

buildtemplate(M20Al,lm,50,center=FALSE) 

 

LMdata<-digitsurface(P12Al,12, ptsize=1,center=FALSE) 

 

Thanks in advance!


-Karen
